title: introduce compact cross-sdk connector + backwards-compat shims for retry/auth ergonomics
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We have three divergent retry/reauth implementations across TypeScript, Python and Go that produce subtle UX differences (backoff defaults, token refresh hooks, streaming reconnect semantics). This PR introduces a compact, language-agnostic connector interface and lightweight compatibility shims so each SDK can adopt the same surface with minimal breaking changes. The goal is to: 1) reduce maintenance cost by consolidating core retry logic, 2) improve streaming reconnect ergonomics (resume/cursor semantics), and 3) make cross-SDK behavior predictable for users migrating between languages.

Summary of changes (single-pass string): Added a compact connector spec and reference implementation in internal sdks/connector; plumbed connector adapters for TypeScript (sdks/typescript/src/retry/compactConnector.ts), Python (sdks/python/redwood/retry/connector.py) and Go (sdks/go/retry/connector.go). Introduced compatibility shims so older init patterns continue to work (examples and changelogs updated). Normalized backoff defaults to exponential with jitter and capped max_delay=60s. Streaming: added a small resume token handshake and a typed cursor wrapper in each SDK so streamed generators/iterables expose consistent .resume() semantics. CI/workflow: expanded sdk-matrix to run cross-lang streaming integration tests and bumped matrix to include go1.21, node20, python3.12.

Migration notes: Existing code using previous retry factories will continue to work via shims but will log a deprecation warning for one release cycle. To opt in to the new connector explicitly: pass { connector: compactConnector() } (TS/Go/Python examples in docs). If you rely on custom token rotation hooks, the connector supports a single async refreshToken() callback; adapters translate older refresh hooks automatically.

Testing: Added unit tests for new connector in each SDK, integration tests for streaming resume across language pairings, and CI job that runs a three-way compatibility matrix (TS <-> Python <-> Go) for the most common streaming handshake scenarios. Local perf: compact connector reduced median token generation CPU time by ~7% in our micro-benchmarks (see bench notes).

Rollback: Reverting the feature branch restores previous behavior because shims were applied; however a revert should be coordinated with SDK consumers if they already adopted the named connector import.

Related: ENG-2041 (cross-sdk retry consolidation), ENG-2090 (streaming ergonomics).

review_comments: Riley Chen (review): We should make the backoff window configurable per-instance; hardcoding a cap can bite us for low-latency use-cases.
Asha Kapoor (author): Agreed; added optional maxDelay param and default to 60s. Documented in migration notes.
Matt Bell (review): TypeScript examples rely on older .stream() iterator shape; ensure adapter preserves .resume() and iterator close behavior.
Asha Kapoor (author): Adapter wraps legacy iterator and exposes .resume() delegation. Added integration tests that verify both shapes.
Sonia Patel (review): CI failure on first run showed flakiness in Go streaming test (race on token cache). Can you add a lightweight mutex around cache access?
Asha Kapoor (author): Added sync.Mutex to connector.go token cache, re-ran CI — passed on subsequent run.
release_notes: Introduce compact cross-sdk connector (opt-in, backwards-compatible shims). Normalize retry/backoff defaults and add streaming resume cursor across TS/Python/Go. Minor SDK bumps and docs.
